info.title: HOODCHAN Brawl API
info.description: Backend for HOODCHAN Brawl, built on the PFP Brawl engine (see ADAPTERS.md) running the HOODCHAN adapter (config.key: "hoodchan"). Covers three things: (1) ambient win/loss/leaderboard stats per token ID, namespaced per adapter via the `adapter` param so two different collections' token #42 never share a record - unauthenticated by design, a fun social signal, not a verified competitive record; (2) the remote-lobby (room code) flow for exchanging fighters between two devices - `lobby/join` enforces a real on-chain ownerOf() check, `lobby/complete` does not yet require signed/agreeing results from both sides (see docs/PLAN-2026-09-engine-rebuild.md); (3) the mint pipeline - completed matches are queued and minted by a cron job using an operator-held key (`MINTER_PRIVATE_KEY`), never a player's wallet; players never sign a transaction, only read-only wallet connect (`eth_requestAccounts`) and (for result submission going forward) off-chain EIP-191 messages. `api/mint-cron.js` is the only route requiring a secret (`CRON_SECRET` bearer, set by Vercel Cron); every other route here is unauthenticated. This deployment's own data lives under the `hoodchan` namespace in its own Redis store (KV_REST_API_URL/TOKEN, set independently per Vercel project). Source: https://github.com/Pixelpushin/hoodchan-brawl.

200.description: Ranked fighters, highest win count first

get.summary: Get the head-to-head win record between two tokens
get.description: Order of tokenIdA/tokenIdB in the path doesn't matter - both orderings resolve to the same underlying record. Security: none - unauthenticated public read.

parameters.name: adapter
parameters.description: Which adapter's namespace to read from (matches that adapter's config.key). Defaults to onchainhoodies.

200.description: Head-to-head win record for this pairing

wins.description: Win count for this pairing keyed by token ID (as a string)

post.summary: Record the outcome of a completed vs-AI match for one token
post.description: Called by the game client itself when a vs-AI match ends. Security: none - unauthenticated, not designed to resist abuse, treat resulting stats as an ambient/fun signal rather than a verified record. When opponentTokenId is present this also updates that pairing's head-to-head record (see /api/rivalry/{tokenIdA}/{tokenIdB}), and a win also updates the adapter's leaderboard (see /api/leaderboard). Does not touch the mint pipeline - see /api/ai-match-complete for the mint-triggering vs-AI route.

adapter.description: Which adapter's namespace to write to (matches that adapter's config.key). Defaults to onchainhoodies.

post.summary: Record a completed vs-AI match and enqueue an on-chain soulbound mint
post.description:
Called by the game client when a vs-AI match ends with two chosen NFTs. Writes stats (same as /api/match-result) and enqueues a soulbound match-record mint that api/mint-cron.js picks up within a minute and sends from the operator-held minter key - the player never signs or pays for this. Security: wallet1 must sign (EIP-191 personal_sign) the message
  HOODCHAN Brawl AI match result
nft1: HOODCHAN #<nft1>
nft2: HOODCHAN #<nft2>
winner: HOODCHAN #<winnerId|none>
address: <wallet1>
issued: <issuedAt>
which the server rebuilds from the validated fields and verifies (10-minute freshness, single-use). In addition, the money-relevant checks are enforced server-side before anything is queued - live ownerOf() confirms both wallet1/wallet2 actually hold nft1/nft2 (RPC failure -> 502, never treated as confirmed), wallet1 !== wallet2 is rejected, one mint claim per unordered token pair (30-day idempotency lock, 409 on repeat), a 3-mints/24h per-wallet cap (429 on repeat), and a fail-closed 5-requests/10min-per-IP rate limit (429, and Redis being down throttles rather than waves requests through).

wallet1.description: NFT owner address for player 1 (not a TBA); must actually own nft1, verified live on-chain

wallet2.description: NFT owner address for player 2 (not a TBA); the AI opponent's owner in the common case; must actually own nft2, verified live on-chain; must differ from wallet1

adapter.description: Stats namespace only; the mint itself always targets the HOODCHAN contract. Defaults to the deployment's ADAPTER_KEY.

issuedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the client put in the signed message; must be within the last 10 minutes (60 s future skew allowed) and must match the signed bytes exactly.

signature.description: EIP-191 personal_sign signature (0x…) over the message described in this route's description, produced by the wallet in `wallet`/`wallet1`. Single-use: a replayed signature is rejected with 409.

400.description: Invalid body (bad address, bad token ID, winnerId not one of nft1/nft2, wallet1 === wallet2)

403.description: Ownership mismatch - wallet does not own the claimed token

409.description: This token pair already has a mint claimed or pending

429.description: Per-IP rate limit or per-wallet daily mint cap exceeded

502.description: Could not verify ownership (RPC unavailable), or could not record match result

post.summary: Create a new remote-PVP room and return a room code
post.description: Room state stored in Redis with a 10-minute TTL. Security: none - unauthenticated; anyone can create a room.

post.summary: Join a remote-PVP room, claiming p1 or p2
post.description: Security: on-chain ownership check enforced - when both wallet and tokenId are provided, this route calls ownerOf(tokenId) via api/_lib/chain.js against Robinhood Chain and 403s if the wallet doesn't actually hold that token; RPC failures return 502 rather than failing open. A `signature` field is accepted in the body for future EIP-191 verification but is not validated server-side yet. Uses a compare-and-set write against the lobby record to avoid two simultaneous joins clobbering each other.

wallet.description: 0x-prefixed address, required alongside tokenId to trigger the ownerOf check

signature.description: Accepted but not yet verified server-side

200.description: Joined; lobby status flips to ready once both slots are filled

403.description: Wallet does not own the claimed token, or side already claimed by another wallet

502.description: Ownership check failed (RPC unavailable) or corrupted room state

get.description: Pure read, no writes (besides a TTL keep-alive while a room is still filling). Security: none - unauthenticated, but wallet exposure is staged: before status reaches 'ready', a filled slot returns only { present: true, tokenId }, no wallet at all; at 'ready' and later, wallets are returned truncated (0xabcd…1234) unless the caller sends their own wallet in the `x-brawl-wallet` header and it matches p1 or p2 in this room, in which case both full addresses are shown. Signatures and internal timestamps are never exposed at any stage.

parameters.name: x-brawl-wallet
parameters.description: Caller's own wallet address; unlocks full (non-truncated) wallets for the two participants once the room is ready

200.description: Lobby state: status (waiting/connected/ready/complete) plus p1/p2 as null | {present, tokenId} | {wallet, tokenId}

post.summary: Report a remote-PVP match's result and enqueue an on-chain soulbound mint
post.description:
Signed, both-players-must-agree result submission. Each client signs (EIP-191 personal_sign) the message
  HOODCHAN Brawl result
room: <ROOMCODE>
winner: HOODCHAN #<winnerId|none>
loser: HOODCHAN #<loserId|none>
score: <p1Score>-<p2Score> in <roundsPlayed>
address: <wallet>
issued: <issuedAt>
The server rebuilds that message from the validated fields (never trusts client text), verifies the signature recovers `wallet`, requires `wallet` to be one of the room's two registered (live ownerOf-checked) players, enforces the 10-minute freshness window, and consumes the signature (single-use). The first submission is stored (200 {recorded:false, waitingFor}); when the second side submits and winner/loser/scores agree, an atomic finalize claim runs the stats writes (adapter-namespaced keys, so the leaderboard/stats/rivalry/recent endpoints see them) and enqueues the soulbound mint (200 {recorded:true, minted:'queued'}); disagreement marks the room disputed and writes nothing (200 {recorded:false, disputed:true}). Completed or disputed rooms answer 409. Rate limit 10/10min per IP, fail-closed.

wallet.description: Submitting player's wallet (must be the room's p1 or p2)

issuedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the client put in the signed message; must be within the last 10 minutes (60 s future skew allowed) and must match the signed bytes exactly.

signature.description: EIP-191 personal_sign signature (0x…) over the message described in this route's description, produced by the wallet in `wallet`/`wallet1`. Single-use: a replayed signature is rejected with 409.

get.summary: Cron entrypoint: drain the mint queue and send soulbound mints
get.description: Called by Vercel Cron every minute; scans mintqueue:* entries written by /api/ai-match-complete and /api/lobby/complete and mints each via api/_lib/mint.js using the operator-held MINTER_PRIVATE_KEY, then increments the community bar total. Security: bearer secret required - Vercel sends `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`; any other/missing Authorization header is rejected with 401, and the route 503s if CRON_SECRET isn't configured. This is the only route in this API that requires a secret.

get.summary: Get the set of opponent pairings this wallet has already minted a soulbound record against
get.description: Used by the collection picker to grey out already-fought pairings (a second mint for the same pair is also rejected on-chain). Security: none - unauthenticated public read.

400.description: wallet must be a valid 0x address

get.summary: Get the community bar total (cumulative minted match records) and milestone status
get.description: bar:total is written only by the mint pipeline (api/mint-cron.js); this route is read-only. Security: none - unauthenticated public read; cached 60s.

get.summary: Server-side IPFS gateway proxy for collection art
get.description: Races a dedicated Pinata gateway (if configured) and public gateways to fetch a CID, avoiding client-side CORS/rate-limit failures. Security: none - unauthenticated public proxy, read-only against IPFS.

post.summary: Upload a K.O. share card PNG to Vercel Blob
post.description: Body is raw PNG bytes (Content-Type: image/png), max 3MB, validated against the PNG magic-byte signature (Content-Type alone isn't trusted). Returns the public blob URL for use with /api/share. Security: none - unauthenticated public write; KO cards are public by design. Rate limited 5 requests/10min/IP (fail-open).

400.description: Content-Type must be image/png, or payload too large

get.summary: Render an HTML page with OG/Twitter/Farcaster meta tags for a share-card image
get.description: Validates `img` is a real Vercel Blob URL (this deployment's own upload host) before trusting it, so this can't be used as an open-graph proxy for arbitrary images. Security: none - unauthenticated public read.

200.description: HTML page with OG meta tags

post.summary: Farcaster frame POST action - redirects to the game
post.description: Security: none - unauthenticated; always 302s to https://fight.hoodchan.org regardless of body.

get.summary: Read the X (Twitter) handle linked to a wallet address, if any

400.description: address must be a valid 0x-prefixed wallet address

get.summary: Start the X OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE flow for a wallet address
get.description: Redirects to X's consent screen; code_verifier is stashed server-side against a one-time `state`. Security: none - unauthenticated (anyone can start a flow for any address; the flow itself only ever links the handle the X account that actually completes it holds - see callback). Requires X_CLIENT_ID/X_AUTH_REDIRECT_URI configured.

400.description: address must be a valid 0x-prefixed wallet address

get.summary: X OAuth callback - exchanges the code, stores the linked handle, redirects home
get.description: Security: state-validated (one-time-use `state` token issued by /api/x-auth/start, looked up in Redis and deleted on use) but otherwise unauthenticated - same ambient/display-label trust model as the match-record API, not an account system. Redirects to /?xLinked=<handle> or /?xLinkError=<reason>.
